name: 38 Oxley Road
description: The site at 38 Oxley Road bore witness to pivotal events in the 1950s that marked Singapore�s transition from a colony to an independent nation.

name: Abdul Gafoor Mosque
description: Abdul Gafoor Mosque's charming architecture stands out amidst the surrounding shophouses in the historic Little India district.

name: Adam Park
address: Junction of Adam Road and Adam Park, near 7 Adam Park
description: Adam park estate was the site of intense fighting between British forces and the invading Japanese army in February 1942, in the last days before the British surrendered Singapore.

name: Al-Abrar Mosque
description: Located on Telok Ayer Street, a short walk from Thian Hock Keng, the Former Keng Teck Whay Building, and the Former Nagore Dargah, Al-Abrar Mosque is one of Singapore's oldest mosques.

name: Alexandra Hospital
address: 378 Alexandra Road, Garden Valley at Alexandra Hospital, Singapore 159964
description: Opened in 1940, the Alexandra Hospital (former British Military Hospital) served as the principal hospital for Britain's Far East Command during World War II. The hospital was the most-advanced and best-equipped medical institution in Singapore and Malaya.

name: Alkaff Upper Serangoon Mosque
description: Alkaff Upper Serangoon Mosque was constructed by the mercantile and landowning Alkaff family to serve the spiritual needs of the local Muslim community at large.

name: Anglo-Chinese School
description: The Anglo-Chinese School (ACS) was founded by Rev. William Fitzjames Oldham in 1886 at a shophouse in Amoy Street. Starting with 13 students, the school aimed to provide an education for the many boys Bishop Fitzjames saw wandering aimlessly in the streets.

name: Armenian Apostolic Church of Saint Gregory the Illuminator
description: The Armenian Apostolic Church of Saint Gregory the Illuminator - commonly called the Armenian Church - is Singapore's oldest Christian church

name: Balestier Plain
address: Balestier Road, Beside Bus Stop No. 50239, Near Ceylon Sports Club
description: Balestier Road, from which Balestier Plain takes its name, was named after Joseph Balestier, a keen botanist and agriculturist who arrived in Singapore in 1834. He was appointed as the first U.S Consul in Singapore in 1836 by then President of the United States, Andrew Jackson.

name: Battle of Bukit Timah
address: Bukit Timah Nature Reserve, near visitor centre, Bukit Timah Hill
description: One of the fiercest military encounters during WWII took place here as the Bukit Timah area held strategic and tactical importance to the Japanese and the British. This site marks Percival's final defence of southern Singapore against the Japanese invaders from the north on 8 February 1942.

name: Battlebox Visitor Centre
address: 2 Cox Terrace Fort Canning Park, Singapore 179622
description: Only guided tours. 2 tours available. THE BATTLEBOX TOUR: Adult: S$18, Child (7-12 years): S$9. Tuesdays to Sundays, including public holidays): 9.45am, 11.00am, 1.30pm, 2.45pm, 4.00pm. OF GRAVES, GUNS & BATTLES: S$32/S$15. Mo, Th 2.00pm

name: Batu Berlayar
address: Labrador Villa Road, Batu Berlayar Point, near Car Park B, Labrador Nature Reserve, Singapore 119187
description: Batu Berlayar ("Sailing Rock"), together with a rock on the opposite shore of Tanjong Rimau, formed a gateway to the west of Keppel Harbour. It was blown up in 1848 to widen the harbour's entrance.

name: Beach Road Police Station
description: In the early 1900s, Singapore grew rapidly and the crime rate rose with the city's expansion. Harold Fariburn - the Inspector - General of Police from 1925 to 1935 - realised that the Police needed a programme of modernisation and expansion. As a result, police stations like the Beach Road Police Station were built around 1930s.

name: Bowyer Block
description: Amidst the modern blocks in the sprawling compound of Singapore General Hospital stands a Neoclassical building with its distinctive clock tower.

name: Bukit Batok Memorials
address: Lorong Sesuai End, Bukit Batok Nature Park
description: Two memorials, one for the Japanese soldiers and the other for Allied Soldiers sat on top on this hill-top. The former was Syonan Chureito, built by 500 Allied Prisoners of War while the latter was a wooden cross that stood behind.

name: Bukit Brown Municipal Cemetery
description: Located in the central area of Singapore, bordering Lornie Road and parts of the Pan-Island Expressway, Bukit Brown Cemetery (BBC) was the first Chinese municipal cemetery in colonial Singapore.

name: Cathedral of the Good Shepherd
description: The Cathedral of the Good Shepherd is Singapore's oldest Catholic place of worship and the seat of the local Roman Catholic archbishop.

name: Central Fire Station
description: The Central Fire Station is the oldest surviving fire station in Singapore and is a living monument to the local firefighting force.

name: Central Sikh Temple
address: Block 269 Queen Street, In front of #01-234, Singapore 180269
description: Also known as the Wadda Gurdwara, this Sikh temple was the first set up in a bungalow at Queen Street in 1912. The temple is now relocated at Towner Road.

name: Changi Beach Massacre
address: Changi Beach Park Lamp Post A2-13 (113), Near Car Park 2
description: Changi Beach was a massacre site of Sook Ching. The Hojo Kempei (Japanese auxiliary military police) machine-gunned many male civilians on this shore on 20 February 1942.

name: Changi Murals
address: 1000 Upper Changi Road North, Side Entrance of Changi Museum, Singapore 507707
description: The Changi Murals was a symbol of hope and faith for prisoners during the Japanese Occupation. It depicted scenes from the Bible, and were painted by Stanley Warren, a Prisoner-of-War.

name: Changi Prison Gate Wall and Turrets
description: Changi Prison was designed to be a maximum security prison to house up to 600 criminals sentenced to long-term imprisonment in British Singapore.

name: Chen Wen Hsi Historic Marker
description: This was formerly the home of Chen Wen Hsi, one of Singapore's pioneer artists. Chen's works mixed Western and Chinese traditions, and continued to influence local artists after his demise in 1991.

name: Chesed-El Synagogue
description: Chesed-El Synagogue on Oxley Rise is one of two synagogues in Singapore, the other being Maghain Aboth Synagogue on Waterloo Street.

name: Chinese High School Clock Tower
description: The Chinese High School Clock Tower Building is the icon of the oldest Chinese-medium high school in Singapore and has been a visual landmark of Bukit Timah Road since its completion.

name: Chui Eng Free School
address: 130 Amoy Street, Far East Square, Singapore 49959
description: Chui Eng Free School was established here in 1854 by the Singapore Hokkien Huay Kuan. It was the second-oldest private Chinese school and also one of the first free educational institutions in Singapore.

name: Chung Cheng High School (Main) Administration Building and Entrance Arch
description: As one of Singapore's oldest Chinese high schools, Chung Cheng High School was among the firsts to make higher education accessible to Chinese youth.

name: Church of Our Lady of Lourdes
description: Known simply as the Indian Church or Tamil Church in the past, the Church of Our Lady of Lourdes is one of Singapore's oldest Catholic churches.

name: Church of Saints Peter and Paul
description: The Church of Saints Peter and Paul is one of the oldest Catholic churches in Singapore that catered to a predominantly Chinese congregation.

name: Church of St Teresa
description: Standing atop a little hill, the Church of Saint Teresa was originally constructed for the spiritual needs of the Hokkien-speaking Catholics living in the town area.

name: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
description: The Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary is one of the earliest Catholic churches built in the suburbs of Singapore.

name: Civilian War Memorial
description: Not far from the Esplanade Park Memorials stands the Civilian War Memorial, the first memorial in Singapore dedicated to the civilian victims of the Japanese Occupation (1942-1945).

name: Clifford Pier
address: 80 Collyer Quay, The Fullerton Bay Hotel, Singapore 49326
description: Clifford Pier was the landing point for sea passengers and immigrants who came to seek a new life in Singapore. It is also known as "Red Lantern Pier" for the red lamps that hung here.

name: College of Medicine Building
description: The College of Medicine Building is located at the rear of the Singapore General Hospital's compound, next to Tan Teck Guan Building.

name: Custom House, Maxwell Road
description: This was the headquarters of Singapore Customs from 1932 to 1989. The building also housed the Film Censor's Office and the Maxwell Road Post Office.

name: Deng Xiaoping Historic Marker
address: Beside Anderson Bridge, on the grounds of the Asian Civilisations Museum
description: Originally known as Deng Xiansheng and his school name Deng Xixian, Deng Xiaoping was born on 22 August 1904 in Guang'an County, Sichuan Province. In 1920, Deng left forÂ studies in France. His six-year stay in France proved to be a turning point in his life.

name: Ee Hoe Hean Club
description: Founded in 1895, it is one of the oldest millionaires club in Singapore. The club was the centre of the Chinese Salvation Movement in Southeast Asia from 1937-1942. Originally located at Duxton Hill, it moved to Club Street before settling at this location in 1952.

name: Esplanade Park Memorials
description: Prior to the first land reclamation in 1843, the original shoreline of Singapore ran across the present Padang.

name: Execution of Captured Rimau Commandos Historic Marker
address: Dover Road, Beside Bus Stop No. 19059, Near NUS U-town Dover Road Entrance
description: Operation Rimau ("tiger" in Malay) was the second Allied commando attack on Japanese ships in Keppel Harbour. It failed, and ten commandos were beheaded by the Japanese near Dover and Clementi Roads.

name: Farrer Park
address: Walkway to Block 11, Gloucester Road, near Farrer Park MRT Station Exit D
description: Farrer Park was the site of the first race course in Singapore, and continued to be a venue for numerous sporting events. It was a site for political gatherings and demonstrations in the 1940s and 1950s.

name: Force 136 Historic Marker
address: Lornie Road, Beside zig-zag bridge to Pavailion, MacRitchie Reservoir Park, Singapore 297732
description: Force 136 was a British secret service team that operated in Malaya during the Second World War. One of the agents was Lim Bo Seng, who led Gustavus V Operation in 1943. His grave is in the vicinity.

name: Former Admiralty House
description: Surrounded by several ancillary buildings and facilities on a sprawling estate, the Former Admiralty House used to accommodate key military commanders based in Singapore.

name: Former Attorney-Generals Chambers (now Parliament House Block C)
description: Tucked away in a corner near the Padang is a beautiful structure that once housed the Attorney-General's Chambers.

name: Former Cathay Building (now The Cathay)
description: The Art Deco facade wall fronting the modern glass architecture of The Cathay is the remnant of what used to be Malaya's tallest building.

name: Former City Hall
description: Located in the heart of the Civic District, the Former City Hall served as an important government office in Singapore.

name: Former Command House
description: The stately Former Command House is located near Bukit Timah Road, a major road constructed during the mid-nineteenth century and one of the last defences against the invading Japanese troops in 1942.

name: Former Convent of the Holy Infant Jesus Chapel and Caldwell House (now CHIJMES)
description: Owing to its central location, the Convent of the Holy Infant Jesus was also affectionately referred to as the Town Convent in the past.

name: Former Empress Place Building (now Asian Civilisations Museum)
description: Situated at the mouth of the Singapore River, the Former Empress Place Building was an important government building in Singapore up to the 1980s.

name: Former Ford Factory (now Memories at Old Ford Factory)
description: Built atop a little hill, the Former Ford Factory has been a visual landmark in Bukit Timah since its completion in 1941.

name: Former Fullerton Building
description: The former Fullerton Building is a prominent landmark situated at the mouth of the Singapore River.

name: Former Hill Street Police Station
description: Nicknamed the 'Police Skyscraper' in the past, the Former Hill Street Police Station is prominently located at the junction of Hill Street and River Valley Road.

name: Former House of Tan Yeok Nee
description: Standing out prominently from its modern surroundings, the Chinese-style Former House of Tan Yeok Nee is the sole survivor of the 'Four Grand Mansions' built in the late nineteenth-century.

name: Former Kandang Kerbau Hospital
description: Built between the 1930s-1950s, these blocks are representative buildings of the former KKH and showcase the hospital�s instrumental role in advancing midwifery, maternal, and gynaecological care in Singapore.

name: Former Keng Teck Whay Building
description: Once home to one of Singapore's oldest self-help organisations, the Former Keng Teck Whay Building is situated next to Thian Hock Keng.

name: Former Ministry of Labour Building (now Family Justice Courts)
description: The Former Ministry of Labour Building is located not far away from the Former Thong Chai Medical Institution and Tan Si Chong Su.

name: Former Nagore Dargah
description: The Former Nagore Dargah is situated on the historic Telok Ayer Street, a short distance from Telok Ayer Chinese Methodist Church, Al-Abrar Mosque and Thian Hock Keng.

name: Former Nanyang University Library and Administration Building, Memorial and Arch
description: Nanyang University, affectionately known as Nantah, was the first Chinese-language university in Southeast Asia and the second university in Singapore.

name: Former Parliament House and Annex Building (now The Arts House)
description: The Former Parliament House is likely to be the oldest surviving building in Singapore.

name: Former Raffles College (now NUS Campus at Bukit Timah)
description: Located next to the Singapore Botanic Gardens, the Former Raffles College is well hidden from the public eye.

name: Former Saint Joseph's Institution (now Singapore Art Museum)
description: Saint Joseph's Institution is the oldest Catholic boys' school in Singapore and was founded by the Christian Brothers (formally known as the Institute of the Brothers of the Christian Schools)

name: Former Singapore Conference Hall and Trade Union House (now Singapore Conference Hall)
description: The Former Singapore Conference Hall and Trade Union House was constructed to house the headquarters of the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) as the fulfilment of an election promise.

name: Former Siong Lim Temple (now Lian Shan Shuang Lin Monastery)
description: The traditional architecture of Lian Shan Shuang Lin Monastery - or 'Twin Grove Monastery on Lotus Hill' - stands out amidst the modern high-rise apartment blocks in the Toa Payoh neighbourhood.

name: Former St James Power Station
description: The Former Saint James Power Station was the first coal-fired power station on the island.

name: Former Sun Yat Sen Villa (now Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall)
description: Sun Yat-sen Nanyang Memorial Hall is one of the few surviving examples of villas that were once common sights in British Singapore.

name: Former Supreme Court
description: Amidst the colonial buildings and skyscrapers of the Civic District rises the copper-green dome of the Former Supreme Court.

name: Former Tanjong Pagar Railway Station
description: The Former Tanjong Pagar Railway Station was previously the southernmost terminal station of the Federated Malay States Railways.

name: Former Tao Nan School (now The Peranakan Museum)
description: A stone's throw from the Armenian Church is a century-old building that used to house Tao Nan School, the first modern Chinese school in Singapore.

name: Former Telok Ayer Market (now known as Lau Pa Sat)
description: Affectionately known as Lau Pa Sat ('Old Market') by generations of Singaporeans, the Former Telok Ayer Market was one of Singapore's oldest markets.

name: Former Thong Chai Medical Institution
description: Home to the first free traditional Chinese medical clinic for the poor in Singapore, the Former Thong Chai Medical Institution testifies to the Chinese pioneers' spirit of mutual assistance and their generosity towards the poor and needy.

name: Fort Canning Command Centre
address: 2 Cox Terrace, Battlebox Entrance, Fort Canning Park, Singapore 179622
description: Fort Canning Command Centre was the site where Lieutenant-General Arthur Percival and his commanders decided to surrender Singapore to the Japanese on 15 February 1942.

name: Fort Siloso
description: Fort Siloso was one of the many coastal fortifications built around the 19th century by the British and remains the most intact fortification in Singapore.

name: Fuk Tak Chi
address: 76 Telok Ayer Street, Far East Square, Singapore 48464
description: This building housed Fuk Tak Chi ("Fu De Ci" in Mandarin), one of the Singapore's oldest Chinese temples, from the 1820s to 1994. It was later converted into a museum.

name: Future site of Science Centre Singapore
Gan Eng Seng School
address: Junction of Telok Ayer Street and Cecil Street, Landscape Plaza
description: In 1885, Gan Eng Seng founded a free school for poor boys in Singapore. Initially named the Anglo-Chinese Free School, it was among the earliest schools to offer a bilingual education. The school moved to its first new building about 50 metres behind Telok Ayer Chinese Methodist Church in 1893. It became known as Gan Eng Seng School in 1923.

name: Gate of Hope
description: From a small gate here, the compassionate sisters of the Convent of the Holy Infant Jesus took in many abandoned infants and children. A replica, named "Gate of Hope", was installed here in 1996.

name: Geylang Serai
address: Blk 1 Geylang Serai, Main entrance of Geylanf Serai Market and Food Centre, Singapore 402001
description: Geylang Serai is a social centre for the Malay community in Singapore. It was originally filled with lemongrass ("serai" in Malay) plantations between the 1890s to early 1900s.

name: Goodwood Park Hotel (Tower Block)
description: The Tower Wing of the present-day Goodwood Park Hotel was home to the German Teutonia Club, one of the earliest European national clubs in Singapore.

name: Hajjah Fatimah Mosque
description: Hajjah Fatimah Mosque is one of the oldest mosques in Singapore, a rare example of one named after a woman.

name: Havelock Road Camp / River Valley Road Camp
address: 491 River Valley Road, Beside bus stop no. 13059, Valley Point Shopping Centre, Singapore 248371
description: The area bounded by River Valley Road and Havelock Road was occupied by Prisoner-of-War (POW) camps during the Japanese Occupation. Five thousand POWs lived in dilapidated attap huts here.

name: Ho Chi Minh Historic Marker
address: Beside Anderson Bridge, on the grounds of the Asian Civilisations Museum

name: Hong San See
description: Hong San See ('Temple on Phoenix Hill'), perched on the side of Institution Hill off Mohamed Sultan Road, was established by Hokkien immigrants from Nan'an (or Lam Ann) County in Fujian Province.

name: Indian National Army Memorial
address: Queen Elizabeth Walk Esplanade Park, near Cenotaph
description: The local INA, influenced by Subhas Chandra Bose, was formed in 1942 with Japanese support, with the aim of liberating India from British.

name: Institute of Mental Health
address: 10 Buangkok View, Main entrance of Buangkok Green Medical Park, Singapore 539747
description: The Mental Hospital was completed in 1928 at Yio Chu Kang Road. It was renamed "Woodbridge Hospital" after a nearby wooden bridge, and then "The Institute of Mental Health" after moving here in 1993.

name: Istana Kampong Gelam
description: Within the historic district of Kampong Gelam lies Istana Kampong Gelam ('Gelam Village Palace').

name: Jalan Besar Stadium
address: 100 Tyrwhitt Road, North entrance of Jalan Besar Stadium, Singapore 207542
description: Jalan Besar Stadium was Singapore's main football arena until the National Stadium opened. It also hosted various national events, such as Singapore Youth Festival and National Day Parade.

name: Jamae Mosque
description: Like the nearby Sri Mariamman Temple, Jamae Mosque has been a familiar landmark on South Bridge Road since the mid-nineteenth century.

name: Japanese Propaganda Department
address: 2 Handy Road, Handy Road open space, beside The Cathay, Singapore 220233
description: Formerly housing the British Malaya Broadcasting Corporations before WWII, it was turned into a Japanese propaganda office during the Japanese Occupation. It was later also used by Lord Louis Mountbatten as the headquarters for the Japanese Surrender in 1945.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru Historic Marker
address: Beside Anderson Bridge, on the grounds of the Asian Civilisations Museum

name: Johore Battery
address: 27 Cosford Road, Off Upper Changi Road, Singapore 499549
description: Completed in the late 1930s, Johore Battery was part of Singapore's coastal defence system. It comprised three 15-inch guns known as "monster guns".

name: Jose Rizal Historic Marker
address: Beside Anderson Bridge, on the grounds of the Asian Civilisations Museum

name: Joseph Conrad Historic Marker
address: Beside Anderson Bridge, on the grounds of the Fullerton Hotel
description: Joseph Conrad, the renowned English master writer, was of Polish origin and travelled to Singapore and south east asia during his seafaring days. He made Singapore and Southeast asia better known to the world through his writings.

name: Jurong Town Hall
description: On a hill overlooking Jurong estate, Jurong Town Hall once served as the headquarters of Jurong Town Corporation (JTC, presently JTC Corporation).

name: Jurong-Kranji Defence Line
address: Between Blocks 550 and 551 Jurong West Street 42, Jurong West Neighbourhood Park, Singapore 640551
description: This is an arbitrary defence line from Kranji River to Jurong River, placed to check Japanese advance towards the city from the west.

name: Kallang Airport
address: Junction of Kallang Airport Way and Stadium Link, beside gate to Former Kallang Airport
description: This is Singapore's first purpose-built civil airport. Completed in 1937, the modern-style terminal building symbolised the rapid civil aviation progress then. The airport ceased operations in 1955.

name: Kallang Gasworks
address: Kampong Bugis End, opposite Kallang Riverside Park
description: Built in 1862, Kallang Gasworks was Singapore's first supplier of piped gas. It played an important role in ensuring efficient gas production for Singapore.

name: Kandang Kerbau Hospital
address: Junction of Bukit Timah Road and Tekka Lane
description: Kandang Kerbau Hospital, the birthplace of over 1.2 million Singaporeans, was the largest maternity hospital in the world from the early 1950s to the early 1970s. It was named after the district where it was located. The district around the crossroads formed by Serangoon Road, Selegie Road, Bukit Timah Road and Rochor Road was known in Malay as Kerdang Kerbau.""

name: Katong Antique House 加東古董
Katong Park
address: Meyer Road, Beside Amphitheatre at Katong Park
description: This is one of the oldest parks in Singapore. Built in the 1930s, it was a favourite place for families and couples, with facilities such as swimming bays which extended into the sea and food outlets.

name: Kempeitai East District Branch
address: 1 Orchard Road, Junction of Fort Canning Road and Orchard Road, beside YMCA, Singapore 238824
description: The original building, the YMCA, was used by the East Branch of the Kempeitai (Japanese Military Police) during the Japanese Occupation. Local anti-Japanese suspects were imprisoned and tortured for information here. The building was pulled down in 1981.

name: Keppel Harbour
address: Harbourfront Walk End, Promenade between Harbourfront Centre and Vivocity
description: Keppel Harbour has been a thriving maritime gateway for trade since the late 19th century. During the Second World War, Operation Jaywick successfully destroyed seven Japanese ships here.

name: Kranji Beach Battle
address: Kranji Reservoir Park, Kranji Way, near Pavilion area
description: It was here on 9 February 1942 that the Japanese forces suffered a major loss, fighting against the valiant 27th Australian Brigade and the Dalforce.

name: Kwan Im Thong Hood Cho Temple
description: This temple was built in 1884, showcasing a fine example of Chinese temple architecture and traditional craftsmanship. The temple played an important role in providing refuge for the sick, the wounded and the homeless during the Japanese Occupation.

name: Kwong Wai Shiu Hospital Heritage Gallery
Labrador Battery
address: Labrador Villa Road, Near History Walk, Labrador Nature Reserve, Singapore 119187
description: This is one of the surviving gun emplacements in Singapore today. The battery has two 6" 16-ton guns facing south, which aided the Malay Regiment in the Battle for Pasir Panjang by firing high explosive shells at the advancing Japanese troops along the coastals.

name: Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum
Lower Barracks
address: 100 Eu Tong Sen Street, Junction of Pearl's Hill and Eu Tong Sen Street, opposite Pearl's Centre, Singapore 59812
description: From 1881, Sikh men began arriving in Singapore as part of the Straits Settlement Police�s Sikh Contingent. Along with the Upper Barracks at the top of this hill, this 5-Storey building was completed in 1934 to house the men.

name: Lower Peirce Reservoir
address: Old Upper Thomson Road, Beside Jetty, Lower Peirce Reservoir Park
description: This is Singapore's second reservoir, constructed after water demand outgrew the capacity of MacRitchie Reservoir. It was known as Kalang River Reservoir when it opened in 1912.

name: MacDonald House
description: Located not far from the Istana and the Former Cathay Building, MacDonald House has a relatively plain and unadorned facade that does not appear to be exceptionally striking.

name: MacRitchie Reservoir
address: 181 Lornie Road, At the foot of Hilltop, Macritchie Reservoir Park, Singapore 297732
description: Singapore's first reservoir was officially opened in 1878 as the Impounding Reservoir, to supply freshwater for the growing population. It has also been a popular place for recreation over the years.

name: Maghain Aboth Synagogue
description: Located in the former Jewish neighbourhood, Maghain Aboth Synagogue is the oldest surviving synagogue not only in Singapore, but also in Southeast Asia.

name: MAS Gallery
description: interactive gallery detailing history and function of MAS along with education of Singaporean finance

name: Merdeka Bridge
address: Merdeka Bridge, Nicoll Highway, beside lamp post 88F
description: Merdeka Bridge, declared open on 17 August 1956, was constructed to ease traffic congestion. Its name reflects Singapore's aspirations for independence ("merdeka" in Malay) then.

name: Methodist Girls' School
address: Junction of Selegie Road and Short Stree, Beside 100 Selegie Road, Singapore 188308
description: Methodist Girls' School began in 1887 as Tamil Girls' School in a shophouse at Short Street with nine Indian girls.

name: Middle Road Church
description: Built between 1870-75, the Middle Road Church was first known as the Christian Institute. When it was officially inaugurated as the Malay Church in 1894, it became the first Straits Chinese Methodist Church in Singapore.

name: Nagore Durgha Indian Muslim Heritage Centre

photos.author: Choo Yut Shing from Singapore, Singapore

name: National Museum of Singapore
description: With its wide facade and large dome, the National Museum of Singapore has been a prominent landmark on Stamford Road for over a century.

name: National Theatre
address: Junction of River Valley Road and Clemnceau Avenue, Beside Fort Canning Park
description: Officially opened on 8 August 1963, this theatre was built to commemorate the attainment of Singapore's self-government in 1959. It was demolished in 1986 due to structural reasons.

name: Objectifs - Centre for Photography and Film
Omar Kampong Malacca Mosque
description: Established in 1820, Omar Kampong Malacca Mosque is Singapore's oldest mosque. In the 1850s, the original timber structure made way for the current building to accommodate the mosque's growing needs.

name: Our Tampines Gallery
description: gallery within the Tampines library, detailing Tampines' heritage

name: Outram Road Prison
address: Outram Park MRT Station, Exit B
description: Outram Road Prison was the main jail in Singapore until Changi Prison opened in 1937. Thereafter, it became a remand prison, housing opium addicts, juvenile delinquents, and political detainees.

name: Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation
address: 65 Chulia Street, North Tower OCBC Headquarters, Singapore 49513
description: OCBC Bank was formed in 1932 through the merger of three Hokkien banks. It was originally located at China Building which featured a prominent Chinese-style roof and classical elements on its faÃ§ade.

name: Pasir Panjang Battle
address: Vigilante Drive, Kent Ridge Park, beside Car Park B
description: The Battle for Pasir Panjang, where the harbour and British military depots were the coveted gains, marked one of the last battles for Singapore. It lasted from 12 to 14 February 1942.

name: Pasir Panjang Machine-Gun Pillbox
address: Junction of Pasir Panjang Road and Science Park Road, Beside Shell Petrol Station
description: This pillbox lay within the area guarded by the 1st Battalion of the Malay Regiment during the Second World War, to protect key installations in the Southern area, such as Alexandra Military Hospital.

name: Pearl's Hill School
description: Pearl's Hill School began in 1876 at Cross Street as the Singapore Chinese Branch School. It was among the first English elementary schools established by the colonial government.

name: Peoples' Defence Force Headquarters
address: Beach Road, Former Beach Road Camp, South Beach Development
description: In the early days of the SAF and Singapore's independence, the Singapore Infantry Regiment and the PDF shouldered the duties of national defence. The Beach Road Army Camp played a significant role in the transformation.

name: Pondok Peranakan Gelam Club
description: Singapore's last pondok (communal lodging house) was located here from 1932 to 2000. It served the welfare of Baweanese immigrants from the Gelam province of Indonesia's Bawean Island.

name: Prinsep Street Presbyterian Church
description: Prinsep Street Presbyterian Church is one of Singapore's oldest Presbyterian churches.

name: Pulau Sejahat
address: Changi Beach Park Lamp Post A2-13 (113), near Car Park 2
description: Pulau Sejahat was designated as a British defence outpost. The military encampment on the island included gun emplacements, water tanks and observation towers.

name: Punggol Beach Massacre
address: Punggol Road End, Beside Jetty at Punggol Point Park
description: Punggol Beach was a massacre site of Sook Ching. Several men were killed by the Hojo Kempei (Japanese auxiliary military police) on this beach on 28 February 1942.

name: Queen Elizabeth Walk
address: Junction of Promenade Linking Esplanade Theatres and Queen Elizabeth Walk, Esplanade Park
description: This was the site of sporting activities in the early days and became popular with families. In 1953, as part of the Coronation Celebrations, the seafront promenade was refurbished and renamed Queen Elizabeth Walk.

name: Queenstown Historic Marker
address: Between Blocks 46-2 and 46-3 Commonwealth Drive, Singapore 140462
description: Queenstown was built in 1960s to meet housing shortage in Singapore after the Second World War. It is Singapore's first satellite town â€“ an estate with amenities to meet residents' needs.

name: Raffles Girls' School
address: 50 Stamford Road, Junction of Stamdord Road and Armenian Street, beside Lee Kong Chian School of Business, Singapore Management University, Singapore 178899
description: Raffles Girls' School began in 1844 as a girls' department in Singapore Institution (today Raffles Institution), and became independent in 1879. It was located here from 1928 to 1979.

name: Raffles Hotel
description: Raffles Hotel is one of the most well-known luxury hotels in Singapore and the oldest surviving establishment of its kind on the island.

name: Raffles Institution
address: 252 North Bridge Road, Junction of North Bridge Road and Stamford Road, beside Raffles City, Singapore 179103
description: The first school in Singapore, it was founded by Sir Stamford Raffles on 5 June 1823. It was originallly known as "The Institution".

name: Raffles Place
address: Raffles Place MRT Station, Exit A
description: Raffles Place was designated as Singapore's business centre in the 1822 Town Plan. Singapore's earliest banks, merchant houses and department stores were situated here.

name: Reflections at Bukit Chandu
description: Reflections at Bukit Chandu is a World War II interpretive centre developed and managed by the National Archives of Singapore, located on Bukit Chandu (Malay for "Opium Hill").

name: Republic of Singapore Yacht Club
description: Founded in 1826, this club became the Royal Singapore Yacht Club in 1922 under the patronage of the Prince of Wales, and was renamed the Republic of Singapore Yacht Club in 1967 with the first president of Singapore, Yusof bin Ishak as it patrons.

name: Sakya Muni Buddha Gaya Temple
description: Vutthisara, a monk from Thailand, founded the temple in 1927. This site is selected as both Indians and Chinese in an area predominantly settled it. It houses a Buddha statue of 15m talls and weighing 300 tonnes.

name: Sarimbun Beach Landing
address: 69 Jalan Bahtera, Beside Ministry of Education of Jalan Bahtera Adventure Centre, Singapore 719920
description: On 8 February 1942, Japanese forces first landed in Singapore on this beach.

name: Scentopia
description: Learn how perfumes are made

name: Seletar Airfield
address: Beside 1 Piccadilly Circus, near Former Seletar Camp Gate, Bus Stop No. 68111, Singapore 797640
description: Seletar Airfield was the British Royal Air Force's main base in the Far East, equipped to protect the Sembawang naval base. Indian Prisoners-of-War were interned here during the Japanese Occupation.

name: Sentosa Beach Massacre Site
address: 27 Bukit Manis Road, Former Berhala Reping Artillery Post, Serapong Course Road, Course 4, Sentosa Golf Club, Singapore 99892
description: Surrendered British Gunners awaiting Japanese internment buried some 300 bullet-ridden corpses washed ashore on Pulau Blakang Mati, now known as Sentosa.

name: Silat Road Sikh Temple
description: This temple was built in 1924 on Silat Road (today Jalan Bukit Merah). It was also known as the Police Gurdwara (a Sikh place of worship) as its congregation was mostly made up of Sikh policemen.

name: Sime Road Camp
address: Junction between Adam Road and Sime Road, near Bus Stop No. 41141
description: Sime Road Camp was the Combined Headquarters of the British Army and Air Force during the Second World War, until the headquarters relocated to Fort Canning Command Centre.

name: Sime Road Machine-Gun Pillbox
address: Sime Road, Lamp Post 32, near Singapore Island Country Club (Island Location) Entrance
description: This pillbox was located inland to provide fire cover and defence for key installations in Bukit Timah during the Second World War.

name: Singapore Armed Forces Warrant Officers' and Specialists' Club
address: Beach Road, Former NCO Buildings, South Beach Development
description: The British Government built the clubhouse in 1951 for British non-commissioned officers. It was handed over to Singapore Government when the British pulled out in 1969.The SAF WOSE club was formed in 1974 and was formerly known as the SAF NCO Club until it was renamed in 1994.

name: Singapore Badminton Hall
description: Singapore Badminton Hall was built to host international badminton tournaments. In 1962, it was a vote-counting station for the Referendum on Singapore's merger with Malaya, Sabah and Sarawak.

name: Singapore Chin Kang Huay Kuan
description: Established in 1918 by Chinese Immigrants from the Jin Jiang County of southern Fujian Province, it was the headquarters of the Overseas Chinese Mobilisation Council, formed in 1941 to help Singapore's defence against the Japanese.

name: Singapore Chinese Girls' School
description: Singapore Chinese Girls' School began in 1899 at Hill Street. It was founded by Straits Chinese pioneers to provide quality education for girls. The school was located here from 1925 to 1994.

name: Singapore Polytechnic
address: 12 Prince Edward Road, Bestway Building, Singapore 79212
description: Established in 1954, Singapore Polytechnic is the first technical institution in Singapore to train skilled labour. The Prince Edward Campus began operations on 3 November 1958 with 2,800 students.

name: Singapore River Bridges: Cavenagh Bridge, Anderson Bridge and Elgin Bridge
description: Cavenagh, Anderson and Elgin Bridges are the three most historic and architecturally impressive bridges that span the Singapore River. Collectively, they illustrate Singapore's growth as a trading port and flourishing city. Located at the historic mouth of the Singapore River, the bridges symbolically connected Singapore with the world as they facilitated the trade and transport links necessary for the growth of the city.

name: Sook Ching Inspection Centre
address: Beside Block 532 Upper Cross Street, Junction of Upper Cross Street and South Bridge Road, Singapore 50532
description: This site marks one of many temporary registration centres set up by the Kempeitai(Japanese Military Police) to screen anti-Japanese Chinese.

name: Sri Krishnan Temple
description: This temple was built in 1870 and is one of the oldest Hindu temples in Singapore.

name: Sri Mariamman Temple
description: Together with Jamae Mosque, Sri Mariamman Temple - Singapore's oldest Hindu temple - is an enduring icon on South Bridge Road which is a part of Chinatown.

name: Sri Perumal Temple
description: Formerly known as Sri Narasimha Perumal Temple, Sri Srinivasa Perumal Temple is the first Hindu temple in Singapore dedicated to Sri Perumal, the Hindu deity more commonly known as Vishnu.

name: Sri Senpaga Vinayagar Temple
description: This temple was built by Ceylon Tamils. It began in an attap shed under a champak ("senpaga" in Tamil) tree in 1875, located near the discovery site of a statue of Vinayagar (the deity Ganesha).

name: Sri Thendayuthapani Temple
description: Sri Thendayuthapani Temple, commonly referred to as the Chettiars' Temple, is one of Singapore's oldest Hindu temples dedicated to Murugan, the Hindu deity who is also known as Sri Thendayuthapani.

name: St Joseph's Church
description: Saint Joseph's Church on Victoria Street was the headquarters of the Portuguese Mission in Singapore.

name: St. Andrew's Cathedral
description: Saint Andrew's Cathedral is Singapore's oldest surviving Anglican place of worship and is the seat of the Anglican bishop of Singapore.

name: St. George's Church
description: Saint George's Church is situated in the quiet environs off Minden Road, a short distance from the bustling shopping district of Orchard Road.

name: St. Margaret's School
address: 99 Wilkie Road, St. Margaret's Primary School, Singapore 228091
description: St. Margaret's School began as a girls' home at North Bridge Road in 1842, to rescue girls who were homeless or being sold to slavery.

name: Sultan Mosque
description: Formerly the royal mosque of the Sultan of Johor, Sultan Mosque represents the solidarity and unity of Muslims in Singapore.

name: Syonan Jinja
address: Junction between Adam Road and Sime Road, near Bus Stop No. 41141
description: Syonan Jinja was built in 1942 in memory of the Japanese soldiers who died fighting in the invasion of Singapore. Ceremonies for significant events were held here until it was destroyed after the war.

name: Tan Si Chong Su
description: The history of Tan Si Chong Su ('Ancestral Hall of the Tan Clan') is inextricably linked to the influx of Chinese immigrants into Singapore during the late nineteenth century.

name: Tan Teck Guan Building
description: Standing beside the College of Medicine Building is a smaller, two-storey building known as Tan Teck Guan Building.

name: Tan Tock Seng Hospital
address: 11 Jalan Tan Tock Seng, Sinaran Drive entrance of Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Singapore 308433
description: This hospital was founded in 1844 by Tan Tock Seng, a philanthropic Hokkien Chinese pioneer, for the poor and destitute. Here, several firsts in Singapore's medical history were achieved.

name: Telok Ayer Chinese Methodist Church
description: Originally known as the Chinese Methodist Church, Telok Ayer Chinese Methodist Church was the first church established to cater exclusively to the spiritual needs of the Chinese Methodist community.

name: The Archeological Dig and Exhibition Area
The First Public Dental School and Public Clinic
address: 5 Second Hospital Ave, Link Bridge between National Dental Centre Singapore and Health Promotion Board, Singapore 168938
description: Dental Education and modern dentistry in Singapore began here in 1929. The original Clinic and Dental School of the King Edward VII college of Medicine had its beginnings on this site in the Norris Block of the General Hospital. In 1938, the clinic expanded into a purpose-built facility adjacent to Norris Block. The Japanese military occupied the clinic from 1942 to 1945.

name: The Founding of Boys' Brigade in Singapore
address: 77 Prinsep Street, Prinsep Street Presbyterian Church, Singapore 188649
description: Singapore's first company of the Boys' Brigade was formed here on 12 January 1930. From a small company of 12, the Boys' Brigade in Singapore has since grown to a strength of more than 100 companies.

name: The Istana and Sri Temasek
description: Shielded from the bustling Orchard Road by a sprawling green lung, the Istana ('Palace' in Malay) is the official residence of the President of the Republic of Singapore.

name: The Padang
description: The Padang is one of the oldest open spaces in Singapore for public recreation and a commemorative space for people to gather, witness and participate in key milestones of Singapore�s history.

name: Thian Hock Keng
description: Thian Hock Keng ('Palace of Heavenly Happiness') is one of Singapore's oldest Hokkien temples.

name: Tou Mu Kung Temple
description: Tou Mu Kung Temple is the oldest temple in Singapore dedicated to the Taoist deity Jiu Huang Ye ('Nine Emperors' or 'Ninth Emperor').

name: Trinity Theological College
description: Trinity Theological College was born out of the camaraderie and spirit of Christianity experienced by the heads of the Anglican, Methodist and Presbyterian Churches when they were interned at Changi Prison during the Japanese Occupation. Founded on 4th October in 1948, it was the first theological college set up to nurture leadership for the churches in Singapore and Malaya.

name: United Chinese Library
description: United Chinese Library was founded by Dr Sun Yat Sen on 8 August 1910 at North Boat Quay, to spread revolutionary ideas and garner support for Dr Sun's revolution in China.

name: United Engineers Limited
address: 81 Clemenceau Avenue, River Valley Road Entrance of UE Square, Singapore 239920
description: UEL was founded in 1912. It led major construction projects that contributed to Singapore's urbanisation and economic growth, and built many iconic structures including the Former Supreme Court.

name: United Overseas Bank
address: 80 Raffles Place, UOB Plaza One, Singapore 48624
description: On 1 October 1935, UOB opened for business at the Bonham Building in Raffles Place. Over the years, it grew to become one of Singapore's leading banks.

name: Upper Barracks
description: This 3-Storey building, along with the Lower Barracks, on Pearl�s Hill were built in 1934 specifically as residence for the Sikh Contingent of the Straits Settlement Police.

name: Upper Seletar Reservoir
address: Beside Lookout Tower, Upper Seletar Reservoir Park, Mandai Road Track 7
description: Singapore's third reservoir was constructed in 1920 to meet the increased demand for freshwater in Singapore. The iconic lookout tower was added to the reservoir in the 1960s.

name: Victoria Memorial Hall
description: Designed by colonial engineer, John Bennett, the theatre portion of the Victoria Theatre and Concert Hall was built as a Town Hall in 1862 which housed the Municipal Offices.

name: Victoria Theatre and Concert Hall
description: In the heart of Singapore's historic Civic District stand the magnificent Victoria Theatre and Victoria Concert Hall with the iconic clock tower.

name: Withdrawal to Singapore
address: Admiralty Road West, WOODLANDS WATERFRONT PARK, NEAR LAMP POST 1R-32
description: During the Second World War, the last Allied military troop in Malaya withdrew to Singapore through the Causeway on 31 January 1942, after losing Malaya to the Japanese.

name: Yeung Ching School
address: Land Parcel Beside 65 Club Street, Singapore 69439
description: Yeung Ching School began in 1905 as a private school for Cantonese children. Apart from conducting classes in the day, it offered night classes to children who were poor or overaged.

name: Ying Fo Fui Kun
description: Not far from Former Nagore Dargah on Telok Ayer Street is Ying Fo Fui Kun, Singapore's oldest Hakka clan association.

name: Yueh Hai Ching Temple
description: Dwarfed by modern skyscrapers in the heart of the Central Business District is one of Singapore's oldest Chinese temples, Yueh Hai Ching Temple.
